s1.syndrome_frame: Painful erosive skin lesion around a stoma site with suprabasal epidermal splitting and acantholysis
salient_findings: Painful, erosive lesion around the stoma on the anterior abdominal wall
Epidermal erosion with suprabasal epidermal splitting and acantholysis on histopathology
Intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 throughout epidermis on direct immunofluorescence
key_facts: Patient has a 10-year history of Crohn disease
Patient had total proctocolectomy and ileostomy due to intermittent bowel obstructions
Painful, erosive lesion developed around the stoma 5 weeks after surgery
No additional cutaneous or mucosal lesions were present
Microbiological cultures were negative
Histopathology showed suprabasal epidermal splitting with acantholysis
Direct immunofluorescence showed intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 throughout epidermis
High levels of IgG autoantibodies against desmoglein 1 and desmoglein 3 were detected

shortlist.label: Pemphigus vulgaris
shortlist.why_kept: High levels of IgG autoantibodies against desmoglein 1 and desmoglein 3, suprabasal epidermal splitting with acantholysis

shortlist.label: Paraneoplastic pemphigus
shortlist.why_kept: Painful erosive lesion around stoma site, presence of autoantibodies against desmoglein 1 and desmoglein 3

shortlist.label: Pemphigus foliaceus
shortlist.why_kept: Autoantibodies against desmoglein 1, clinical presentation of erosive skin lesion

shortlist.label: Bullous pemphigoid
shortlist.why_kept: Erosive skin lesion, presence of autoantibodies, although less likely due to suprabasal epidermal splitting

shortlist.label: Pemphigus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Autoantibodies against desmoglein 1, clinical presentation of erosive skin lesion, although less common

raw.rationale: The presence of suprabasal epidermal splitting with acantholysis, intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 throughout the epidermis, and high levels of IgG autoantibodies against desmoglein 1 and desmoglein 3 are characteristic of Pemphigus vulgaris

rejected.label: Paraneoplastic pemphigus
rejected.why: Typically associated with underlying neoplasms, which are not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Pemphigus foliaceus
rejected.why: Characterized by subcorneal epidermal splitting, not suprabasal splitting as seen in this case

rejected.label: Bullous pemphigoid
rejected.why: Typically involves subepidermal blistering, not suprabasal epidermal splitting

rejected.label: Pemphigus erythematosus
rejected.why: A variant of Pemphigus foliaceus, which does not match the histopathological findings in this case
